answer: Make every seat prove a living custodian on demand. Each night a beacon fires at a random hour; in nine minutes the seat must photograph its cedar crate with a fresh pigment stripe, mixed from a code given that instant, against its grain on file. One operator can script thousands of wallets but cannot stay awake, mix paint, and handle ten thousand crates at once. Forging photos means copying grain for months and buying pigment that leaves a trail. The attacker pays ten thousand crates, night shifts, and traceable orders, none parallelizable. An honest agent spends a minute a night.
